newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 8.

text.p: Sakura Bank Ltd plans to expand its lending to financially-troubled drug company Green Cross Corp by an initial 9.3 billion yen in December. It will also ask Sanwa Bank Ltd, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd and other banks to help the company.

Sony Corp expects to have increased its consolidated operating profit by 30 percent to 305 billion yen for the business year ending March 1997 from a year earlier, helped by strong sales of electronics products and the yen's weakness. Its consolidated sales are also expected to have increased by 16 percent to 5.35 trillion yen for the period. The forecast is based on an average exchange conversion at 110 yen to the dollar.

Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd expects to record a pre-tax loss of 70.3 billion yen in the business year to March 31, 1997 after disposing of bad assets. It will be the first loss by Mitsui Fudosan since its listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 1949. It is considering writing off 10 billion yen worth of bad assets by the business year ending March 1998.
It may also sell property held by a subsidiary to Tokyo Broadcasting System Inc for about 20 billion yen as part of a plan to restructure group operations.

Yokohama Rubber Co Ltd plans to set up a new computer system to share information on manufacturing and developing tyres by 2000. It will also end its technical cooperation ties with a South Korean tyre maker, and sell its shareholding in the firm in response to increasing competition between the two companies overseas.
